scope: Verify whole OBJECTS rollback, same-writer retry and typed readback for IMAGEDEF callback rejection and every calibrated core IMAGEDEF OBJECTS allocation point.

behavior: The existing IMAGEDEF failure/retry control covers entity-stage rejection and consumer OBJECTS callback validation/bad_alloc after the core has staged NOD, GROUP, IMAGEDEF dictionary, reactor, and IMAGEDEF records.

A calibrated ASCII/Binary control measures allocations between the end of ENTITIES and the adapter OBJECTS callback, then injects std::bad_alloc at each measured allocation offset on the successful core OBJECTS path with a generated IMAGEDEF as the only added object family.
Each core allocation failure occurs before the adapter callback; the OBJECTS record scope and whole-file transaction preserve the existing destination and clear derived entity identities.
The same writer retries after every one-shot allocation failure; a fresh typed DXF import verifies IMAGE and IMAGEDEF data in both encodings.
The allocation injector disables itself when it fires to avoid cascading failures during error reporting. No repository DWG/DXF fixtures are added and no support claim is established.

normalFocused.coverage: ASCII/Binary callback validation plus calibrated core IMAGEDEF OBJECTS all-allocation-offset failure sweep, destination preservation, derived identity rollback, same-writer retry after each failure, and typed IMAGE/IMAGEDEF readback.

coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.result: PASS in ASCII and Binary DXF
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.counts: 7 allocations in the no-image baseline; 18 allocations with the generated IMAGEDEF path; 11 additional allocations attributable to the IMAGEDEF OBJECTS path. Every offset 0 through 17 is injected in turn for the full path.
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.injection: A fresh writer runs at each allocation offset. Each injection is observed exactly once before the consumer OBJECTS callback, then that same writer retries with injection disabled and produces typed IMAGE/IMAGEDEF readback.
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.diagnostic: The current build reports emit-failure because the bounded reserve path normalizes the injected bad_alloc; the assertion also permits allocation-failure if a platform path propagates it.

limitations: The sweep covers all calibrated allocation offsets on the generated IMAGEDEF path; independent core OBJECTS builders and other staged families remain open.
DRW::reserve may normalize bad_alloc into a generic emit-failure diagnostic. The test proves failure atomicity and retry, not diagnostic precision for every allocation site.
Generated round-trip evidence does not qualify native consumer semantics, physical producer breadth, or independent interoperability.
next: Inject allocation failures into independent core OBJECTS builders, then extend failure/retry coverage to other staged families and audit source lifetime, platform numeric/string policies, and scoped concurrency.
